finds.quote: The apparatus of Roman public magnitude — the triumphs, the annals, the res gestae of men who thought themselves the subject of history — is available to us mostly as information. The sparrow is available as *feeling*, unmediated, at full strength, two thousand years later. Something in the dead bird outlasted the empire that would not have counted it. That is not a moral about humility. It is an observation about transmission: the small private object, precisely because it asks nothing of the state, carries no dependency on the state's survival.
finds.note: Historical thesis about transmission: the private small object (Catullus' passer poems) survived at full strength where Roman public magnitude survives as information.

finds.quote: No identified evidence exists of Pearsonian Operational Semiotics as a recognized framework in operational research, organizational semiotics, AI/ML, semiotic management, or the generic signs-as-actions literature. **Those are exactly the five neighborhoods the audited 2026-08-25 composition merged into its umbrella entity.** The merger therefore has no basis even in TOS's own reception: composition did not retrieve a broad Pearsonian uptake and mislabel it — it took a small, specific, institutionally real theory and averaged it with fields that never adopted it.
finds.note: Reception-history thesis (negative finding): Pearsonian TOS was not adopted in five named neighborhoods; refutable by evidence of such uptake.
